Let me look at the `read_rice_signed_block` function one more time. I want to focus on the exact OOB read. Let me look at line 867 again:

```c
b = br->buffer[cwords] << br->consumed_bits;
```

When `cwords >= words`, this reads `br->buffer[cwords]`. If `cwords == words`, this reads `buffer[words]` which is the partial tail word. But what if `cwords > words`?

Let me trace through the code one more time, very carefully, focusing on the `process_tail` section.

When we jump to `process_tail` from the main loop via `incomplete_msbs`:
```c
br->consumed_bits = 0;
br->consumed_words = cwords;
```

`cwords` is the index of the word we were trying to read. Since we jumped because `cwords >= words`, `cwords` could be equal to `words`. So `br->consumed_words = words`.

Then `FLAC__bitreader_read_unary_unsigned(br, &msbs)` is called. Since `consumed_words == words`, it reads from the tail. If the stop bit is found, it returns. `consumed_words` stays at `words`.

Then `FLAC__bitreader_read_raw_uint32(br, &lsbs, parameter - ucbits)` is called. Since `consumed_words == words`, it reads from the tail. After reading, `consumed_words` is still `words`.

Then `cwords = br->consumed_words = words` and `words = br->words`. So `cwords == words` and the loop continues.

At line 867, `br->buffer[cwords]` when `cwords == words` accesses `buffer[words]` which is the partial tail word. This is within the allocated buffer.

But wait - what if `FLAC__bitreader_read_unary_unsigned` in the `process_tail` loop reads from the tail and finds the stop bit, but then `FLAC__bitreader_read_raw_uint32` reads from the tail and consumes all remaining bits? Then `consumed_bits == br->bytes * 8`. But `consumed_words` is still `words`. So `cwords == words` and the loop continues.

At line 867, `br->buffer[cwords] << br->consumed_bits` shifts the partial tail word by `consumed_bits` which is now `br->bytes * 8`. This is fine.

But in the next iteration of `process_tail`, `FLAC__bitreader_read_unary_unsigned` is called again. It checks `br->bytes * 8 > br->consumed_bits`. Since `consumed_bits == br->bytes * 8`, this is false. So it calls `bitreader_read_from_client_` which shifts the buffer and resets `consumed_words = 0`. Then `cwords < words` and the loop exits.

So the `process_tail` loop always exits when there are no more bits to read from the tail. And `br->buffer[cwords]` when `cwords == words` is always within the allocated buffer.
